title: The Gravity of Sector Nine
premise: Tamsin Villalobos has spent fifteen years hauling cargo through the contested orbits of Sector Nine, tending a terraforming garden meant for colonists still frozen in cryosleep. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — a voice counting down inside the reactor — Tamsin discovers the dream is a distress signal from one of the two cryo-banks, each holding half of humanity's survivors and controlled by rival factions who have lied to the waking generation for decades. As the reactor's countdown accelerates, Tamsin must choose which bank wakes first, knowing her own mother sleeps in the other. In the end, she refuses the binary: she reroutes the reactor's power to wake both banks slowly, sacrificing the terraformed garden and her own place in it, and the children's dream becomes a shared memory of what was almost lost.
about_author: Felix Crane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for life-support systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they keep a failing greenhouse and insist it's going well.

chapters.title: Cargo for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Tamsin ferries nutrient stock to the Verdance, the sealed garden meant for future colonists, and reflects on fifteen years of hauling supplies for people who may never wake. Her POV establishes the sector's fragile politics between Warden Station and the Halcyon Consortium. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by doubt about whether the sleepers will ever come.

chapters.title: The Children Who Stopped Playing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's young cousin Ilo describes a dream shared by every child in the habitat: a corridor of frost, a heartbeat that counts. Teachers dismiss it; the medics log it as mass suggestion. Tamsin recognizes the dream's geography — it matches Deck Seven of Cryo-Bank A. POV shifts briefly to Ilo. Emotional beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: Two Banks, One Reactor
chapters.summary: Tamsin pulls maintenance records and learns the reactor feeds both cryo-banks on a rotation schedule no one will explain. Warden liaison Osei warns her off investigating; Consortium agent Reyes offers help with strings attached. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: the first sense that loyalty here means picking a side.

chapters.title: What My Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits the manifest archive and confirms her mother, Marisol, sleeps in Bank B — the bank the Wardens quietly deprioritize years ago. Flashback to Marisol's last transmission before boarding. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose; inheritance as both burden and clue.

chapters.title: The Garden Answers
chapters.summary: In the Verdance, Tamsin finds the bioengineered plants growing in patterns matching the children's dream — root systems tracing the countdown numbers. The garden itself seems to be receiving the signal. Tamsin's POV with Ilo present. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Osei's Confession
chapters.summary: Warden Osei admits the original crew split the sleepers by faction allegiance, then falsified the manifests so the waking generation wouldn't know. He begs Tamsin to let the countdown run its course rather than expose the lie. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: betrayal by the people she trusted most.

chapters.title: Reyes's Bargain
chapters.summary: Reyes reveals the Consortium can wake Bank A alone if Tamsin helps seize the reactor core — but only Bank A, and only their chosen list. She shows Tamsin proof that Marisol's pod is already failing. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by desperation; the choice stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Dream Deepens
chapters.summary: Ilo's chapter: the children's shared dream now includes faces — sleepers pressing against frosted glass, mouthing names. Ilo wakes crying a name Tamsin recognizes from the Bank B manifest. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized; the children become messengers neither faction controls.

chapters.title: Sabotage on Deck Nine
chapters.summary: An 'accident' cripples the cargo lift to Bank B. Tamsin suspects the Wardens; evidence points instead to someone inside her own crew. Her POV, tense investigation through the station's underdecks. Emotional beat: paranoia; nowhere feels safe or honest.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Face
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts her oldest friend and crewmate Dov, who has been feeding schedules to the Consortium to guarantee his partner wakes in Bank A. Their argument lays bare the theme: loyalty vs. truth. Dov's POV for the argument's second half. Emotional beat: heartbreak without villains.

chapters.title: Countdown Made Public
chapters.summary: Ilo and the children broadcast the dream across the habitat's school network, forcing every adult to see the frost corridor. Panic spreads; both factions blame each other. Alternating POVs of Tamsin and Osei. Emotional beat: the lie collapses publicly; chaos becomes opportunity.

chapters.title: Into Bank A
chapters.summary: Tamsin infiltrates Bank A with Reyes to verify the failing pods and finds rows of sleepers whose vitals were deliberately misreported. She records everything. Tamsin's POV, claustrophobic and cold. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Reactor
chapters.summary: Tracing the signal to its source, Tamsin discovers the 'dream' originates from the reactor's diagnostic AI, which detected the pod failures years ago and had no one awake enough to tell — except through sleeping minds. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: awe; the machine was the only honest witness.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: The AI unlocks Marisol's final pre-freeze message: she knew about the factional split and hid a full uncorrupted manifest inside the garden's root database, trusting Tamsin would tend it. Tamsin's POV, interwoven with Marisol's recorded voice. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; mother and daughter finally speak across decades.

chapters.title: Faction Firefight
chapters.summary: Wardens and Consortium forces clash at the reactor when the true manifest surfaces. Dov defects back to Tamsin's side mid-battle, buying her time at the cost of his own arrest. Multiple POVs, kinetic action. Emotional beat: loyalty proven not by alignment but by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Choice Presented
chapters.summary: The AI presents Tamsin the impossible math: power remains to fully wake one bank or partially wake both, and the countdown ends in thirty hours. Osei argues for certainty; Reyes for survival of the fittest list. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: the weight of a decision no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: The Children Vote
chapters.summary: Ilo gathers the children, who have lived their whole lives as 'the reason' — and they ask to be the deciders' conscience, not its casualties. They choose the garden over guaranteed rescue: wake everyone slowly, even if it costs them the world they know. Ilo's POV. Emotional beat: the next generation refusing inherited cruelty.

chapters.title: Rerouting the Heart
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Dov, and the AI execute the dual-wake sequence while Wardens and Consortium fight for the manual override. Tamsin physically holds the coupling together as the reactor screams. Climax begins. Tamsin's POV, relentless pacing. Emotional beat: courage as endurance, not heroics.

chapters.title: Burning the Garden
chapters.summary: To power both banks, the Verdance must be drained — fifteen years of Tamsin's care dies in minutes. She walks its rows one last time, releasing the seed vaults into the sector's drift so the garden might take root elsewhere. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into letting go.

chapters.title: First Breath
chapters.summary: Bank A opens. The first sleepers wake coughing and furious and alive — including people from both factions' forbidden lists. Osei resigns rather than enforce the old order; Reyes's superiors recall her, but she delays to help triage. Multiple POVs. Emotional beat: messy, imperfect hope arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Bank B Opens
chapters.summary: Hours later, Bank B thaws. Tamsin waits at the pod bay as Marisol wakes — older than memory, disoriented, real. Their reunion is awkward and unfinished and enough. Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: the payoff of every sacrifice; identity restored through recognition.

chapters.title: Seeds in the Drift
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the habitat rebuilds around shared truth: public manifests, joint governance, children teaching adults the dream's meaning. Tamsin receives a ping — a seed vault took root on a drifting rock near Sector Nine's edge. She signs on to fly out and plant the next garden herself. Tamsin's POV closing the arc. Emotional beat: inheritance renewed; the story ends where it began, hauling cargo toward the unborn.
